incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] 502/503 spike on hosted inference (canary) — 2026-06-18T02:12:01Z. Error rate 22% over 5m. Link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/ingest/canary?from=now-5m&to=now
Sara Li: seeing it, thanks for the ping. which rollout is this?
Raj Patel: canary is the new attention-kernel rollout (kernel-v2) targeted at 10% of traffic for model 'redwood-open-7b'. saw errors correlate with requests > 1024 tokens.
Mike H.: logs show KV cache OOMs on some nodes, stacktrace points to kernel_v2::kv::lookup failing with allocation error.
Sara Li: can we flip traffic back to kernel-v1? what's the fast mitigation?
Raj Patel: two options: 1) flip feature flag 'kernel-v2-canary' to off (immediate routing revert) 2) roll the canary deployment back with deploy-bot. flag toggle is fastest.
Mike H.: I can flip the flag. hitting the console now.
Mike H.: @deploy-bot toggle-flag --name=kernel-v2-canary --env=hosted --value=false
deploy-bot: command received: toggle-flag kernel-v2-canary -> false. Propagation to routing in ~10s.
incident-bot: Status update: flag toggle propagated to 95% of routing nodes. Error rate dropping from 22% -> 4% in EU region.
Sara Li: good. keep monitoring. can we get a quick customer impact estimate? any key tenants affected?
Raj Patel: preliminary: three customers hit hard (EU region, model redwood-open-7b with long-context requests). One reported latency >5s and ~15% request failures in last 8m. Most customers unaffected.
Mike H.: running quick sweep for any crashloop pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l rollout=kernel-v2 | grep CrashLoopBackOff
Mike H.: found 4 pods with OOM kills on worker nodes eu-west-2a.
Sara Li: leave them cordoned and mark for deeper heap/kv config check. We need to rollback the canaryed kernel image and open a deploy revert ticket.
Raj Patel: will open ticket: "rollback/kernel-v2-canary-1769804321" and attach logs.
Raj Patel: ticket created: https://tickets.redwood.internal/INC-2026-9812
incident-bot: Severity: P2 -> mitigated (routing reverted). No active page escalation required.
Sara Li: handoff to Alex for follow-up and postmortem. Alex, can you own the incident until root cause & remediation?
Alex K.: taking it. I'll coordinate with runtime team tomorrow morning and chase down kv allocation regression.
Alex K.: action items: 1) reproduce locally with long-context workload 2) run heap profiler on kv cache 3) add unit test to avoid allocation regression 4) review rollout gating to include long-context smoke tests
Mike H.: also add guardrails: fail fast to kernel-v1 if OOMs or >10% errors in 1m window.
Sara Li: nice. please add a short customer note template. For now ops message: "We rolled back a recent canary kernel rollout after detecting increased errors for long-context requests. Most traffic restored; a small set of EU customers saw transient 5xxs. Investigating root cause and will follow up."
Alex K.: will draft and loop in support.
Raj Patel: saving logs/snippets: ```
2026-06-18T02:09:23Z worker-17 ERROR kernel_v2::kv::lookup: allocation failed for 8.2MB keyval
2026-06-18T02:09:25Z worker-17 OOM Killed process pid=2345 (inference)
```
Sara Li: thanks. add postmortem owners and ETA for RCA?
Alex K.: RCA ETA: 48h, postmortem doc link TBD after RCA. I'll update INC-2026-9812 and assign to runtime team.
incident-bot: final update: flag rollback propagated to all regions at 02:14:28Z; error rate normalized to baseline by 02:17:03Z.
Sara Li: closing the immediate page. Alex, please keep this thread updated with RCA and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
Alex K.: will do. tagging @support for customer comms.
Mike H.: leaving a note to re-run canary with increased replica and long-context smoke tests before any new rollout.
Sara Li: agreed. End of thread.
